title: READOUT: Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent's Meeting with European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maroš Šefčovič
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with EU Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič on April 27, 2026, to discuss the new U.S.-EU Action Plan for Critical Minerals and progress on the 2025 EU-U.S. Joint Statement. The meeting covered economic security priorities, investment screening, addressing overcapacity risks, Iran's threat to the Strait of Hormuz, and U.S. G20 priorities around food and fertilizer supply chains.
key_points: Secretary Bessent and Commissioner Šefčovič discussed the new U.S.-EU Action Plan for Critical Minerals
Progress reviewed on the 2025 EU-U.S. Joint Statement, including EU investments in American autos, pharmaceuticals, and energy
Both officials highlighted joint priorities on economic security, investment screening, and addressing overcapacity production risks
Secretary Bessent raised concerns about Iran's threat to the Strait of Hormuz
U.S. G20 Presidency focus emphasized efforts to keep food and fertilizer supply chains functioning
why_it_matters: The readout signals continued U.S.-EU coordination on trade and economic security, with particular focus on critical minerals supply chains and industrial overcapacity. The mention of Strait of Hormuz concerns introduces potential energy supply risk. For markets, this indicates diplomatic engagement on trade tensions and supply chain resilience, though the readout lacks specific policy details or numbers.
macro_context: The meeting reflects ongoing U.S.-EU efforts to coordinate on trade policy, critical minerals sourcing, and addressing Chinese industrial overcapacity. Strait of Hormuz references signal potential energy supply concerns that could affect oil markets. G20 focus on food and fertilizer supply chains suggests attention to global commodity availability.
